newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices steady amid lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices steady amid lackluster trade.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices finished Wednesday steady against Tuesday's levels in lackluster activity despite a rise in crude oil prices.
Despite expectations of end-users, notably utilities, needing to replenish their oil inventories during the first cold snap of the winter season, level of trades anticipated has not materialise yet.
"Nothing is going on here," noted an East Coast trader.
Despite another pull-back in natural gas futures, physical gas prices were mostly higher today as the Arctic chill was predicted to bear over most of the country until the weekend.
Although cash resid values were flat, forward paper prices fluctuated with gas and crude futures, traders said.
New York Harbor one pct remained in $21.75-22.00 a barrel range, with January paper talked about 50 cents lower at $21.80-$22.00.
High sulphurs in New York held steady from Tuesday, with 2.2 percent still assessed near $18.50.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour grade stayed in the $23.00 area, traders said.
U.S. Gulf Coast one percent was still at $18.50, while three percent notionally held at $16.00-25. January three pct paper edged down 10-25 cents to $16.40-$16.60.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate gas prices discussed in the $4.50-$4.70/mmBtu range Wednesday, compared with Tuesday's $4.60/mmBtu area and NYH one percent resid at a $3.47/mmBtu equivalent.
